messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I want a fair financial share. I haven’t agreed to A buying at a discount, because that would mean I’m subsidizing her. I don’t know what the will says about the house, and I’m not in a hurry to settle it.

My husband and I would like to buy the house at a family discount, but I haven’t settled on a price or terms. I need C’s agreement before we can proceed. I’m concerned we’ll rush into details before all three of us have had a chance to agree.

A payout from the house’s value would probably help me most, as I’d like to start a dance studio. I don’t know what amount or arrangement would be fair yet. I’m not against A buying the house, but I’m not sure we have a plan everyone can agree to. My main worry is having enough to get the studio started.

I don’t have the will or know what it says about the house. Yes, I’d settle what the will says and get a valuation before discussing terms. Price matters, but I still need a fair financial share; I haven’t agreed to subsidize A.

The list looks right. I agree price is central, though the terms matter too. I’d accept finding out what the will says and getting a qualified valuation before discussing terms. I’d like to hear C explain what she considers fair before I suggest a price.

Yes, I’d be happy to start by checking the will and getting a qualified valuation. I don’t have the will and don’t know what it says. I’m not sure it’s simply one number to divide up; that may depend on what the will says and what everyone is entitled to.

I don’t know who has the will or whether there’s an executor or solicitor. To me, fair means my share should reflect what the will says I’m entitled to and a qualified valuation—not a discount that I end up funding.
I don’t know whether there’s an executor or solicitor holding the will. I’m not sure who has it, so perhaps we should ask together who the executor is and request the will from them.

Yes, asking together who has the will and requesting it sounds sensible. I don’t have a figure or date in mind yet; I’d like to understand what’s available before suggesting an amount. The studio is what I’d hope to use my share toward.
